summary: This bill bars state and local officers from arresting or detaining any foreign national inside the United States solely on the basis of an ICC-issued warrant or request, and preempts any state or local law that would allow such action unless Congress passes specific authorizing legislation or the President issues a written national-security certification.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal, state, or local spending levels, appropriations, or budgetary matters. It focuses exclusively on limiting state and local cooperation with the ICC.
No references to taxes, tax policy, rates, or revenue collection appear in the legislation.
The bill does not address healthcare systems, coverage, providers, or related regulations.
No content pertains to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

While the bill references foreign nationals present in the United States, its purpose is narrowly to block state/local enforcement of ICC warrants rather than to alter immigration pathways, border policy, visas, asylum, or deportation rules. The connection is incidental at most.
The legislation has no bearing on reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions address military budgets, defense spending, or armed forces policy.
The bill does not engage with environmental regulations, climate policy, or conservation measures.
No elements relate to welfare programs, entitlements, or social assistance.
The text contains nothing concerning schools, education funding, or school choice.
No references to controlled substances, decriminalization, or drug enforcement.

The bill restricts certain arrests and detentions by state/local officers when based solely on ICC process, but this is a narrow, ICC-specific preemption rule rather than a general reform of sentencing, policing, or rehabilitation policy. It does not meaningfully engage the topic.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
The legislation does not discuss deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No content relates to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The bill does not address foreign assistance programs or funding.
No provisions concern voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
The legislation contains no language on technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance.
Nothing in the bill pertains to workers' rights, unions, or labor policy.
The bill does not engage with religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination law.
